common_policy_assessment.conclusion: The public official evidence does not settle restaurant/KTV access. SAFRA By-Laws §§6.1 and 6.4 say members may bring guests and that where applicable guests are signed in/accompanied. The current membership FAQ says members and family/friends can access most SAFRA-managed facilities. An older reciprocal-partnership document says guests under that arrangement must be accompanied, but this is not a universal outlet-access rule. These sources do not support a blanket exclusion of SAFRA tenants or proof of independent public entry.

sources.evidence: Current by-laws §6.1 permits members to bring guests; §6.4 requires sign-in/accompaniment only “where applicable”. No across-the-board member-only public-entry rule for commercial F&B tenants appears in the cited clauses.

Current FAQ says clubs are open to members and family/friends for most SAFRA-managed facilities and directs visitors to individual facility information. It does not expressly state eligibility for ordinary restaurant/KTV customers.

Official reciprocal arrangement (updated 26 Feb 2024) states all guests in that reciprocal arrangement must be accompanied by SAFRA/HomeTeamNS/NSRCC members. This is a restricted arrangement, not a current universal rule for every customer visiting an F&B outlet; not sufficient by itself to prove exclusion.

results.evidence: Current official SAFRA source confirms a tenant at the corresponding club; unit-level match is exact. Public-facing hours/menus/member offers establish commercial operation but do not prove that a nonmember can access the clubhouse without a member; the current general rule is conditional. No current official source found in this audit expressly says this tenant is member-only or expressly confirms an independent public entrance. Do not remove or mark public based on available evidence.
